root.name: Van Geet Opening: Sicilian Two Knights
root.moves: 1. Nc3 c5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. d4 cxd4 4. Nxd4

overview: 1.Nc3 c5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.d4 cxd4 4.Nxd4 reaches an Open Sicilian with White's queen's knight already on c3. Black usually plays 4...Nf6 and White 5.e4 or 5.Ndb5, giving a Sicilian Four Knights or Taimanov-like game, or 4...e6 and ...Qc7. It plays like a mainstream Open Sicilian and lets White steer toward the Sicilian with the b1-knight developed.

white_ideas.idea: Play e4 and develop with Be3 or g3 in an Open Sicilian set-up
Use the knight on d4 and c3 to pressure d5 and c6

black_ideas.idea: Develop with ...Nf6 and ...e6 or ...g6 as in a Sicilian
Use ...d5 or ...e5 breaks to challenge e4

typical_structures.structure: Open Sicilian: White e4 against Black d6/e6, half-open c-file for Black
Maróczy-style centre if White plays e4 and c4

character.notes: Open Sicilian middlegames; White can steer to sharp or positional paths, Black often has equal chances.

soundness.notes: A sound move order into the Open Sicilian.

structure.notes: Sicilian asymmetry with a half-open c-file for Black.

approach.notes: Mostly a Sicilian by transposition; the Van Geet move order is a respectable but uncommon route.

level.notes: Standard Sicilian plans; the key is knowing the Open Sicilian ideas.

character.reason: Open Sicilian positions can go either way depending on White's set-up; not a forcing main line.

structure.reason: Every Sicilian has an asymmetric centre with a half-open c-file.

approach.reason: A less common route into the Open Sicilian, not a surprise weapon.

level.reason: Standard Sicilian knowledge; plans matter more than lines.

plans.reason: Plans depend on Black's set-up so none is clearly characteristic.
